The leakage current expression Ids is derived from the thermal field emission mechanism. The leakage current noise power spectral density (PSD) expression S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Ids</inf> is derived from the carrier number fluctuation theory. It is proved that S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Ids</inf> is proportional to ID<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</inf>, approximately. The current and noise expressions are verified by available experimental data.

articleTitle: High-speed disturbance-free nonvolatile flip-flop based on complementary polarizers
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid CMOS/magnetic nonvolatile flip-flop (NVFF) for standby-power-critical and quick-startup applications. Different from conventional magnetic NVFFs, which are based on the two-terminal magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ), the proposed NVFF employs the complementary-polarizer magnetic tunnel junction (CPMTJ) to introduce the non-volatility. The writing and sensing circuits of CPMTJ are separately merged into the master stage of the NVFF to perform store and restore operations when the power turns on/off. In addition, the proposed NVFF is designed to operate as fast as the conventional CMOS flip-flop in the active mode. For performance evaluation of the proposed structure, SPICE model of CPMTJ is developed based on the theories of spin-transfer-torque (STT) switching and tunneling magnetoresistance effect, and then simulations are conducted in comparison of the conventional magnetic NVFF. Simulation results show that the proposed NVFF achieves 59% faster storing speed under iso-writing transistor width condition and 57% reduced storing energy for the same storing speed. By utilizing the cancellation of opposite spin-transfer torques, the proposed structure is expected to achieve a fully disturbance-free restore operation. Moreover, a 4GHz toggling speed in the active mode is demonstrated in SPICE pre-layout simulations using 45nm CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Bidirectional multi-level spatial coded exposure CMOS capacitive TIA pixel design
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Over the last decade, computational cameras have demonstrated superior performance in a variety of applications. Currently, optical encoding is implemented using components that are typically not integrated on the image sensor chip. This results in camera systems with large physical sizes, performance compromises, and implementation challenges, particularly in applications where size and power are constrained. In this paper, we propose a complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) pixel structure with bidirectional multi-level spatial coded exposure encoding capability for computational imaging. Based on a capacitive transimpedance amplifier (CTIA) core, the proposed pixel architecture achieves bidirectional multi-level optical encoding, and is compatible with monolithic CMOS implementation. Designed and laid out in a standard 0.13-pm CMOS process, the pixel occupies an area of 13.8 pm × 13.8 pm with a fill factor of 30%.

articleTitle: Design considerations for power efficient continuous-time delta-sigma converters
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Continuous-time Delta-Sigma Modulators (CTΔΣMs) are a compelling choice for the design of high resolution analog-to-digital converters. Many delta-sigma architectures have been published (and continue to be invented). This leaves the designer with a bewildering array of choices, many of which seem to pull in opposite directions. Further, it is often difficult to make a clear comparison of various architectures, as they have been designed for dissimilar specifications, by different design groups, and in different technology nodes. This paper examines various design alternatives for the design of power efficient single-loop continuous-time delta sigma converters.

articleTitle: An Op-amp free SAR-VCO hybrid ADC with second-order noise shaping
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel SAR-VCO hybrid 1-1 MASH ADC, where a passive 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup>-order noise-shaping SAR ADC eliminates Op-amp in the first stage. A VCO-based ADC digitizes the residue of SAR ADC with one additional noise-shaping order in the second stage. The inter-stage gain error is suppressed by a foreground calibration. A prototype ADC is designed in a 65nm CMOS process. The transistor-level simulation results show that 75.7 dB SNDR and 14.9 fj/conversion-step FoM are achieved in the 5 MHz bandwidth at 60 MS/s under 1.0 V supply.

articleTitle: Cross-coupled Gm-boosting technique for two-stage miller-compensated amplifier
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A two-stage Miller-compensated amplifier with cross-coupled G<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>-boosting structure is presented in this paper. The proposed G<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>-boosting cell is able to increase the effective transconductance of the second gain stage such that the bandwidth can be substantially increased. Additionally, the required compensation capacitor is reduced significantly when compared with the classical two-stage Miller-compensated amplifier. Simulated using the device models of a commercial 130-nm CMOS technology, the achieved unity-gain frequency (UGF) and phase margin are 431.12 kHz and 73.2°, respectively, when driving a capacitive load of 1-nF under supply voltages of ±0.6 V. The improvement of the UGF over the classical Miller-compensated amplifier is 8.36 times. Moreover, the required compensation capacitor is reduced by 7.69 times.

articleTitle: Low perfusion algorithm used in wearable oximeter and hardware acceleration
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This paper proposes a simple and efficient algorithm named “fundamental frequency detection and narrow bandpass filtering” to calculate SpO2 in wearable oximeter when it is in low perfusion condition. The two-stage pipeline structure is used to accelerate computing when the algorithm is implemented by hardware logic circuit. Through the FPGA verification, the system can output real-time, continuous calculation, and extract pulse wave from as low as 0.1% perfusion signal then accurately calculate SpO2 value with an error less than 3%. It can entirely satisfy the medical demands.

articleTitle: Mobility variation and threshold voltage shift immunized amorphous-indium-gallium-zinc-oxide pixel circuit
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A mobility variation and threshold voltage (Vth) shift immunized amorphous-indium-gallium-zinc-oxide (a-IGZO) pixel circuit has been proposed for active matrix organic light-emitting diode (AMOLED) display application. The pixel circuit consists of four a-IGZO thin film transistors (TFTs) with a simple driving scheme. The design has been validated to compensate for the mobility variation and Vth shift of the driving TFT based on simulation. The current of organic light-emitting diode (OLED) changes by only 10.1% when the Vth is shifted towards the positive direction by 40% and the mobility is decreased by 10%, while that from a conventional a-IGZO pixel circuit changes by 36.1% under the same condition.

articleTitle: A fast three-level feedback technique in continuous-time delta-sigma modulators
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This paper presents a third order continuous-time (CT) delta-sigma (ΔΣ) modulator with a fast three-level feedback scheme. The proposed technique uses two decorrelated 1-bit quantisers to produce a three-level feedback signal without requiring a decoder in the feedback path thus enabling high-speed operation. An efficient dynamic-element matching technique is also implemented to mitigate the weak non-linearity induced by the element mismatch. Two different approaches of implementing this technique are investigated and behavioral simulations are presented.

articleTitle: Device modeling for circuit simulation in nanometer technology
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Summary form only given. Device modeling has always been the key bridging technology to enable designers to access the new features and performance of the manufacture technologies. Starting from the textbook device models, such as MOS1 to MOS3, and Gummel-Poon, to a series of BSIM models and other standardized models today, device modeling has gone through a long journey to meet the growing needs of circuit designers in IC industry. This work will focus on the major milestones of the classical models and standardized models as well as their application. To the interests of circuit designers, we will emphasis on their primary improvement over their predecessor and the new challenge they brought in for engineering implementation. While discussing the model features and major advantages, we will review what a good model should do and what a designer should know about it before adopting it. Additionally, we will briefly introduce their typical usages in design and major issues to resolve in order to achieve better match between the real silicon and design. A good model can only provide positive potentials. To take the full advantage of it, the modeling process of matching, layout effects, statistical variations and multi-finger effects will all be explored. As most of the model libraries will be made and provided to designers as a black box by foundries, how and what you should know about the libraries will also be discussed.

articleTitle: Modeling current reduction/or PCM cell with thermal buffer layer
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: In this work, a model is developed for RESET current reduction calculation for phase-change memory (PCM) cell with thermal buffer layer. Numerical simulation indicates more significant contribution of the buffer layer on heat generation than on thermal loss, supporting following model development which treats the total cell resistance as the crucial factor. The model is verified by comparison with both finite-element simulation and experimental data, hence is capable to give guidance in future buffer layer design, particularly in estimation for the limit value of current reduction and buffer layer thickness.

articleTitle: Design of an optimized CMOS series-parallel coupled LC quadrature phase oscillator
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This paper presents a complementary CMOS LC quadrature phase oscillator optimized for tuning range and power dissipation. Usage of complementary cross-coupled pair, in addition to series and parallel coupling, helps to reduce the power dissipation while decreasing the tuning range. A method has been proposed for optimizing the trade off between power dissipation and tuning range. With the proposed methodology, a quadrature phase oscillator with center frequency of 16.6 GHz has been designed in standard 65nm-ll technology. Simulation results show 32% tuning range with average power dissipation of 6mW over the tuning range.

articleTitle: A 66-to-76GHz E-band QPLL with amplifier feedback QVCO in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A fully integrated 66-76GHz E-band low phase noise quadrature phase-locked loop (QPLL) is proposed. The quadrature voltage-controlled oscillator (QVCO) with a symmetrical coupling network formed by diode-connected transistors is used to reduce the phase error. In order to improve the oscillation frequency and reduced the phase noise, a feedback network composed of buffer amplifiers and capacitors is introduced to the QVCO. The wide locking-range divider chain of PLL consists of an injection-locked frequency divider (ILFD) with a 3-bit binary-weighted switch-capacitor bank, current mode logic (CML) dividers, and a multiple modulus divider (MMD). The proposed circuit was designed in a 65-nm CMOS process, and the QVCO achieves a tuning range of 16.4% from 66GHz to 76GHz with a phase noise of -97dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset while consuming only 12.5mW. The QPLL achieves an excellent phase noise of -93.2 dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset, consuming 37.1mW of power and with a FoM of -174.4dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: A five-order butterworth low-pass filter with DC offset cancellation for WLAN applications
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This paper presents a five-order Butterworth low-pass filter with DC offset cancellation (DCOC) for WLAN Applications in a 65-nm CMOS process. The low-pass filter employs transconductance cell instead of conventional two-stage amplifiers to avoid internal poles which may otherwise cause the reduction of GBW. In order to achieve an appropriate 1-dB bandwidth of the integral filter, extra parasitic capacitances have been carefully considered. The proposed LPF achieves a maximal 1-dB bandwidth up to 80MHz with tunable gain and bandwidth. The LPF consume 4.2mA of current from a 1.2V power supply. A superior 1dB compression point of -2.57dBm is also achieved while with a noise figure of 27.55dB at 20MHz as a result of a good balance between linearity and noise.

articleTitle: Mixed-signal circuits for the data-driven world
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: In today's world, we have come to depend upon highly sophisticated and tightly interwoven electronic systems that facilitate sensing, communication and computing tasks. However, as we move forward, many grand challenges exist in raising the performance of such systems to the next level. For instance, the energy consumption of most sensors and data transceivers is still far too high to operate autonomously and for extended periods of time. On the other end of the spectrum, the power levels required to run sophisticated machine learning algorithms still appears too large for exponential growth and/or massive deployment. In the past, the desired progress was often fueled by engineering better components and by leveraging the immense improvements delivered by CMOS feature size scaling. For example, mixed-signal designers have invested an immense amount of time to port and optimize data converters from node-to-node and have thereby enabled wider bandwidths at steadily lower conversion energies [1], Similarly, RF designers have leveraged the high transit frequencies of modern devices to enable low-noise RF signal processing up to mm-wave frequencies. As we enter the next stage of innovation, it is becoming increasingly clear that future progress will come from a “top-down,” system-driven approach. The sheer complexity of today's systems provides us with a new degree of freedom wherein the system architecture and their underlying components (and possibly transistors) can be co-designed, thus providing larger gains than those enabled within the usual scaling and porting framework. This talk will provide an overview of my group's research on system-driven mixed-signal design, which is guided by the parallel consideration of theory, systems, algorithms and circuits. For instance, we are researching a number of sensing approaches aimed at “fooling Nyquist” and extracting desired analog-domain information using low-rate and low-bandwidth observations. In a second line of work, we investigate the application of mixed-signal co-processors in machine learning algorithms [2], tailored for example toward low-power image classification.

articleTitle: The effects of O2 annealing on the characteristics of IGMO-based UV photodetector
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: In this work, both the structural and ultraviolet photosensitive properties of amorphous InGaMgO thin film were in-depth investigated. It was found the transmittance of InGaMgO thin film was as high as nearly 90% in the visible spectra region, leading to a large bandgap over 3.5 eV. In addition, it was revealed the treatment of post deposition annealing in oxygen can effectively improve the ultraviolet photosensitive properties of InGaMgO thin film. Particularly, the photodetector based on the 240-min annealed InGaMgO thin film exhibited excellent device performance, for instance, a high responsivity of 2.8×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> A/W and a large photo-dark current ratio of 1.1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. However, some degradations were observed when the annealing time was longer than 480 min.

articleTitle: Electricalperformance of multilayer MoS2 transistor with ALD HfTiO gate dielectric
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Electrical performance of MOS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> transistor, especially carrier mobility, can be greatly improved by screening the Columbic scattering by a high-k gate dielectric. In this work, Ti is incorporated into HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> to form HfTiO dielectric with a higher permittivity, which leads to further enhancement of the screening effect and thus carrier mobility. The effects of annealing ambient (N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) on the electrical performance of ALD HfTiO back-gated multilayer M0S2 transistor are investigated, and a highest mobility of 31.1 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/(V-s) is achieved for the ΝΗϊ-annealed sample. However, different from the HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gated MOS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> transistor, the HfTiO gated device exhibits larger off current and subthreshold swing. This is probably attributed to a smaller conduction-band offset between HfTiO and MOS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>.

articleTitle: Exposure optimization for multi-bit quanta image sensor with ultra-small well capacity
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: The effect of ultra-small well capacity is serverely impacting the performance of image sensors fabricated in advanced complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technologies. Therefore, a new sensing paradigm is required to effectively design pixels at the nanometer scale. In this paper, we present a noise and quantization model for the multi-bit quanta image sensor (Mb-QIS). Using the model to analyze the Mb-QIS, we found that an optimal exposure exists that can minimize the error in photon counting. This result is useful for the design and operation of Mb-QIS based image acquisition systems.

articleTitle: Electrically tunable bandgaps in 2D layered materials
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: We demonstrate a novel bandgap engineering approach in a new class of 2D layered materials, semiconducting transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs). Our approach does not require sophisticated growth systems and the bandgap size of the channel material can be dynamically adjusted during the device operation to meet the requirement of a specific application. We will show that the transfer characteristics of a double-gated bilayer MoS2 field-effect transistor (FET) device can continuously change from semiconducting to metallic behavior with increasing gate field, indicating a dynamically reducing bandgap. In photoluminescence measurements, we also observe that the peak associated with the direct bandgap of MoS2 evolves into two resonances under electric field with one peak continuously shifting to lower energies, which is consistent with the interlayer transition induced bandgap reduction observed by transport.

articleTitle: Comparative study of InGaZnO thin-film transistors with single and dual NbLaO gate dielectric layers
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Amorphous InGaZnO thin-film transistor using NbLaO gate dielectric with low La content is prepared and shows acceptable performance with a carrier mobility of 15.7 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>V<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. Moreover, the gate-dielectric/InGaZnO interface can be improved by inserting a buffer layer of NbLaO with higher La content between the gate dielectric and InGaZnO layer, thus resulting in better device performance in terms of higher carrier mobility (28.5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>V<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>), lower threshold voltage (2.5 V), higher on current (252 μA) and smaller hysteresis (0.4 V). Therefore, the HNbLaO is a potential candidate as buffer layer for improving the electrical performance of InGaZnO thin-film transistor.

articleTitle: A speculative clock and data recovery architecture for multi-gigabit/s series links
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This paper presents a speculative architecture of a digital phase-locked loop (DPLL)-based clock and data recovery (CDR) for high-speed receiver in series links. This proposed system removes pipeline stages and reduces propagation delays, as a result, the latency of the loop decreases, which improves the loop stability and jitter tolerance without sacrificing loop bandwidth. This system can realize locking the phase to 1/32 UI and the frequency to 30.51 ppm/lsb, with maximum frequency offset of +/− 6836ppm.

articleTitle: MoO3 nanoplatelets based Schottky diode for low-noise sensors in harsh envionments
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: High-temperature harsh environments demand sensors with thermodynamically stable properties. This paper presents a thermal dynamically stable, low noise Schottky diode based on nanostructured MoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> nanoplatelets. Diode I-V characteristics, barrier height, and series resistance under different temperatures were investigated. Low diode turn-on voltage enables low power operation. MoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> nanoplatelets with length, width, and thickness of 6.7 μm, 3.1 μm, and 0.4 μm provide a significantly improved surface area-to-volume ratio, which is advantageous in high-sensitivity sensor applications.

articleTitle: A 0.048ns/°C delay generator with variation self-calibration structure(VSCS) for HVICs
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A fully on-chip delay generator with a PVT variation self-calibration structure (VSCS) is proposed in this paper. To eliminating the delay variation and ensuring the signal integrity, a proportional to absolute temperature (PTAT) current and a proportional to supply voltage (PTSV) current is adopted in the VSCS. In addition, a bias circuit consisting of positive and negative temperature coefficient resistors is developed to obtain the temperature compensated delay. HVIC adopting the proposed delay generator is implemented in a 0.5 μm 600V Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS (BCD) process. Measured results show that the average temperature coefficient of the proposed delay generator is 0.048ns/°C.

articleTitle: Analytical drain current model for long-channel double-gate negative capacitance junctionless transistors using Landau theory
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: An analytical drain current model was proposed for long-channel double-gate negative capacitance junctionless transistors (DG NC JLTs) with a metal-ferroelectric-insulator-semiconductor structure. The analytical model was derived by solving Poisson's equation, Pao-Sah equation and Landau-Khalatnikov equation. It was shown that the off-state current could be significantly lowered and the on-state current could be improved simultaneously by employing the ferroelectric gate dielectric. The related working principle and physical mechanism were also discussed in detail. The proposed model is suitable for the compact modeling because it is valid for the depletion, flat-band and accumulation regions without any auxiliary variables or functions. The developed DG NC JLTs have a great potential for low-power applications.

articleTitle: Scaling challenges and solutions beyond 10nm
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: 10nm and beyond nodes face significant challenges in pitch scaling and delivering better chip performance at iso power. Increased parasitics and variability due to gate pitch (CPP) and metal pitch scaling require significant innovation in materials, patterning, conformal, higher aspect ratio filling and high selectivity atomic layer etching. Multi-pattern lithography with regularity and restrictive design rules have allowed us to move far beyond 193i single patterning capabilities. However, continued pitch scaling at advanced node will require EUY, at the least, on few critical layers. Innovation such as air gap insertion is in not only a backend metal solution but also in frontend of processing to reduce parasitic capacitance and poses significant challenges in manufacturing. Advanced device architectures such as GAA and Tunnel FET nanowires transistors will further add their own set of manufacturing challenges at advanced nodes in terms bending free suspended channels, conformal deposition and etching of gate stack materials, spacer formation and source/drain epitaxy. In reality, industry will rise to these challenges with innovation and yet be pragmatic in choosing innovation that meets high volume manufacturing requirements.

articleTitle: A 6.5-GHz digitally-controlled oscillatorwith supply sensitivity of 0.0071%-fDCO/1%-VDD
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This paper presents a 65nm CMOS 6.5GHz digitally-controlled oscillator (DCO) with static and dynamic supply sensitivity of 0.00138%-f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DCO</sub>/1%-V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</sub> and 0.0071%-f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DCO</sub>/1%-V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</sub> respectively. By regulating the supply current of DCO, the proposed technique achieves high supply-noise rejection performance. In addition, the proposed DCO has a strong immunity against process and achieves satisfied performance at different corners. The proposed DCO system achieves a phase noise of -107.4dBc/Hz @1MHz and -130.1dBc/Hz @10MHz offset from the carrier and operates from 6.3 GHz to 6.8 GHz, while consuming 3.2mW from a 1.2V supply at 6.5 GHz.

articleTitle: A high-efficient and wide-bandwidth supply modulator using power switch controlled technique
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A high efficient and wide-bandwidth supply modulator with power switch controlled technique (SMPSC) is presented in this paper. The supply modulator offers dynamic output voltage for RF PA power supply application. Improving the efficiency of the RF PA in RF transceiver system. The parallel architecture of supply modulator has better efficiency and wide output bandwidth. And has the capability of outputting large load current. SMPSC technique follows voltage level of input envelope signal to change output power switch of the switching converter and improve the efficiency. The proposed supply modulator has been fabricated with 180nm CMOS process. The chip area is 1.2μm × 1.2μm. SMPSC can work in static output or dynamic output mode. With an input supply voltage of 3.3 V, the output voltage range can be regulated from 0.5V to 3V. The maximum operation input envelope signal frequency is 20MHz. Experimental results demonstrate that the maximum output current is 600mA with 5 Ω equivalent load.

articleTitle: A sub-0.5V charge pump circuit for resistive RAM (ReRAM) enabled low supply voltage nonvolatile logics and nonvoaltile processors
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Many processors that use energy harvesting devices for low-power computing operations and zero-standby-current power-off storage require embedded nonvolatile memory (eNVM) devices and nonvolatile logics (nvLogics) with low-voltage capability. However, conventional eNVMs and nvLogics are unable to perform low-voltage write operations due to a failure on the part of on-chip charge-pump circuits to provide the high write voltage and write current required by NVM devices under low supply voltage (VDD). This study developed hybrid-boost-voltage (HBV) and hybrid-device (HD) schemes for a single-supply charge pump to enable low-VDD operations with sufficient voltage and current for the write operation of ReRAM-based eNVM and nvLogics. A HBV-HD CP fabricated in a 65nm testchip achieved VDDmin ofless than 0.5V.

articleTitle: Invited Talk1
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Silicene, a silicon equivalent of graphene, is predicted to offer a host of exotic electrical properties depending on its phase, underlying surface and external fields. Nevertheless, there is a lack of experimental device studies largely due to air-stability issue. Here we explore challenges and opportunities on silicene device fabrication and characterization. Given our recent progress on encapsulated precaution of air-sensitivity, silicene made its transistor debut. Electrostatic characterization on non-optimized silicene transistors revealed field-effect mobility -100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/V-s with 10× gate modulation in ambient condition. Device optimization is on-going to explore the upper mobility bound achievable and aging evolution of silicene devices. It is likely with further experimental study that monolayer or multilayer silicene can establish a platform for realizing advanced device concepts, e.g. topological bits, on arbitrary substrates beyond what is available in graphene. The unique allotropic affinity of silicene with crystalline bulk silicon suggests a more direct path for the integration with ubiquitous semiconductor technology.

articleTitle: CMOS computational pixel for binary temporal optically encoded high-speed imaging
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Computational imaging has recently attracted much attention due to its excellent potential in delivering advanced capabilities such as motion deblurring and high-speed compressive sensing. However, the development of computational cameras has been limited by the lack of a technology that can efficiently support temporal encoding. Conventionally, temporal encoding is performed by complicated off-chip optics such as split light modulators (SLMs). This results in camera systems with large physical sizes, performance degradation, and high power consumption. In this paper, we propose a complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) pixel design that performs temporal optical binary encoding for on-chip, high-speed computational imaging applications. Compared to conventional high-speed imaging techniques, the proposed CMOS computational pixel is a promising approach for on-chip temporal encoding, enabling simpler camera optics and reduced power consumption.

articleTitle: Ultra-thin and ultra-flexible temperature/strain sensor with CNT nanostrips
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Flexible electronic devices have attracted much attention nowadays. Flexible sensors are required to be thin and flexible in order to better attach to the human being for health care. However, connecting parts of many flexible electronic sensors and the outer circuit are not flexible at all. Severe stress concentration exists and often results in cracks and device failure. In this paper, we present an ultra-thin and ultra-flexible temperature/strain sensor with CNT (Carbon Nanotubes) nanostrip connections. The sensor has good linearity (r<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Temperature</sub> =0.997, r<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">strain</sub>=0.976). The connecting part is completely flexible and highly robust.

articleTitle: Near-infrared light emitting diode array based on ordered Si micropillar/InGaZnO-nanofilm heterojunctions
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A novel near-infrared light emitting diode (LED) array based on ordered Si micropillar/InGaZnO-nanofilm heterojunctions was proposed and demonstrated. The pixel resolution of the LED array is 4,885 dpi, corresponding to a pixel pitch of 5.2μm. The fabricated LED array shows good rectification characteristics with small serial resistance. Carrier transport obeys the trap-charge-limited current model. The electroluminescence emission peaks of this LED device are in the near-infrared region, which attribute to the deep defect level Vo in the InGaZnO film and interface traps in the Si-SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> interface, respectively. These results provide important supplementary for Si-based light emitting devices.

articleTitle: Metamateral enhanced folded waveguide slow wave structure for millimeter wave traveling wave tube amplifier
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: We present theoretical design of a high gain traveling wave tube amplifier employing a folded waveguide and metamaterial structure. Metamaterial structures have unique properties such as high effective permittivity and permeability which can be harnessed in a slow-wave structure for enabling strong interaction with an electron beam to produce signal gain. Meanwhile the strong dispersion of the permittivity and permeability creates outstanding frequency selective absorbing ability. The frequency selective properties of the metamaterial structure provide an interesting option to suppress parasitic oscillations usually encountered in a high gain amplifier. A folded waveguide slow wave structure loaded with metamaterial is designed to achieve high gain traveling wave tube amplifier covering frequency from 57 GHz to 66 GHz. The simulated results of the slow wave structure and particle-in-cell simulation results of the device showing the gain and output characteristics are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Chip design of low-power and dual-band voltage control oscillator
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A low power and dual-band (4.36 and 7.54GHz) voltage control oscillator (VCO) is designed and implemented in TSMC 0.18pm CMOS 1P6M process. The supply voltage is 1.2V. This circuit have dual-band tuning range of 7.54∼7.72 GHz and 4.2∼4.36 GHz at power consumption is 4.32 mW and 4.2mW respectively. And frequency at 4.36 GHz and 7.54 GHz, the phase noise at 1 MHz offset is −120.8 dBc/Hz and −115.48 dBc/Hz respectively. After calculation, the figure of merit is −186.7 dBc/Hz and −187.35dBc/Hz. The layout size is 0.763 × 0.781 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Memory — The N3XT frontier
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Computer architecture is going to change in the coming decade because today's architecture has severe limitations in energy efficiency and latency for memory access [1].

articleTitle: Numerical simulations of nonlinear current-voltage characteristics of nano-channels: A benchmark study
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: The intrinsic coupling of ionic and fluidic transport processes in nano-channel devices, particularly those with weak overlap of electrical double layers (EDLs), leads to strongly nonlinear current-voltage characteristics. Physics-based numerical simulations are desirable for rational design of such devices, but care must be taken to ensure the simulated nonlinearity is not from numerical artifacts. This benchmark study compares nano-channel simulations based on two different device simulators, PROPHET and COMSOL Multiphysics. Good agreement is observed in general, confirming the existence of significant nonlinearity in such devices. The numerical methods and simulation parameters are also discussed.

articleTitle: A reconfigurable UHF CMOS voltage multiplier
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A reconfigurable ultra-high-frequency (UHF) voltage multiplier (VM) is proposed and presented in this paper. By taking the substrate power loss of the silicon wafer into account, the mathematical functions of the output voltage and power-conversion efficiency of the proposed reconfigurable UHF VM with the different series and parallel combinations are found. A reconfigurable UHF VM is realized in a standard 180-nm CMOS technology. The presented analysis is proven by the well-matched calculated with the different series and parallel combinations are found. A reconfigurable UHF VM is realized in a standard 180-nm CMOS technology. The presented analysis is proven by the well-matched calculated and measured results.

articleTitle: Circuit design in nano-scale CMOS technologies
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Summary form only given. Moore's law has led CMOS technology scaling well into nano-scale regime now. Relentless feature size reduction along with innovations in transistor architecture and new material has created both challenges and opportunities for circuit designers. The technology scaling is no longer just about geometric reduction but more about innovations in the use of new materials and transistor architectures. Meanwhile, circuit design in deeply scaled CMOS technologies requires increasingly more innovative approaches over conventional design to fully capture the scaling benefits in power and performance while continuing to lower product cost. In this talk, an overview on the landscape of current technology scaling will first be presented along with future directions. The talk will then explore many advanced circuit design techniques that are important to achieve product-level scaling benefits. It will start with Static-Random-Access-Memory (SRAM), the work-horse for embedded memories in all product applications. The state-of-the-art read-write-assist (RWA) techniques in SRAMs will be fully examined in the context of achieving adequate margins for ever-lower voltage operation. Analog and mixed signal (AMS) circuits have long been considered “not-scalable” due to many unique design requirements and process sensitivities. In this talk, several novel digital-assist techniques are explored to illustrate how they can help achieve excellent power, performance, and area scaling in some common AMS circuits such as phase-lock-loop (PLL) and high-speed serial 10. Adaptive design concept has become more important in advanced circuits today to augment the process variations and minimize design sensitivities. A couple of design examples will be given to demonstrate the benefits of these advanced circuit techniques. To further improve system-level performance, more intelligent product integration schemes are proven to be essential in addressing specific product needs, such as memory bandwidth. Some advanced product design examples, including integrated-voltage-regulator and in-package-memory, will be given to illustrate how they can improve power and performance at system levels. In conclusion, as CMOS technology scaling continues, novel circuit topologies and product integration schemes will play an increasingly more important role to achieve optimal scaling benefits in the future.

articleTitle: Toward high-performance electronics based on carbon nanomaterials
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Single-walled carbon nanotubes are promising to replace silicon as the channel material for high-performance electronics near the end of silicon scaling roadmap, due to their superb electrical properties and intrinsic ultrathin body. Despite the remarkable progress of CNT device and circuit developments recently, many challenges are still required to be overcome in order to realize a practical logic technology. In this invited talk, the progress on both CNT device, material processing, and circuit integration will be reviewed. I will also discuss most significant challenges from technology points of view.

articleTitle: Nanostructured TiO2 Schottky diode with large surface area for chemical sensors
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Despite decades of research, achieving high sensitivity for chemical sensors still remain a challenge. This paper presents a technique for fabricating nanostructured TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> Schottky diodes with a large surface area for chemical sensing applications. The technique is based on hydrothermal synthesis, where the crystallographic phase and surface morphology of the sensing film can be controlled via NaOH concentration during fabrication and post-fabrication annealing temperature. Material properties are analyzed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD). Diode I-V characteristics and barrier height, which corresponds to its turn-on voltage, have been measured and analyzed. Unlike conventional diode implementations, the fabricated Schottky diode exhibits a barrier height that ranges from 1.10 to 1.19 eV, due to the formation of different crystallographic phases and surface morphologies of the TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanostructures. Large surface area and low turn-on voltage holds great potential for high-sensitivity, low-power chemical sensing applications.

articleTitle: A 10GHz analogphase interpolator based on a novel quadrature clock generator
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A 10GHz analog phase interpolator (PI) in Global Foundry 65nm CMOS technology has been presented. The PI mainly consists of the quadrature clock generator (QCG) and the phase Mixer. Different from the traditional divider, the QCG produces 4-phase clocks without reducing the clock frequency. As a result, it reduces the frequency of PLL from 20GHz to 10GHz, which can largely save the power consumption of the clocking system. Compared with the traditional QCG, the proposed QCG achieves a lower output phase error and has a better tolerance of delay variation. With the delay changing from 18ps to 36ps, the output phase error of the proposed QCG keeps within ±4°. Besides, the simulated worst phase step error of the phase Mixer is smaller than 0.2LSB. The whole phase interpolator has the worst phase step error smaller than 0.3LSB. The average power consumption of the QCG and the phase Mixer are 6.14mW and 4.14mW respectively, with a 1.2V supply voltage.

articleTitle: A CMOS high frequency pulse width modulation integrated circuit
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: In this work, a high frequency pulse width modulation (PWM) integrated circuit (IC) designed and implemented in a commercial 0.35 μm CMOS process is presented. Based on natural sampling method, the proposed PWM IC can generate both a PWM signal and its inverse for arbitrary frequencies up to 5 MHz. The PWM frequency can be adjusted via an external clock and an off-chip capacitor. The duty cycle of the PWM signal can be linearly varied from 5% to 95% by changing the input signal. Thanks to its analog triangle wave generation, it provides higher resolution and less quantization error compared to digital implementations. Moreover, the natural sampling based PWM generation offers reduced harmonic distortion over other PWM generation methods. The PWM IC requires a single 5 V supply voltage to operate. The full chip area is 1.4×1.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, including the pad frame. The post-layout simulations reveal that the proposed PWM IC will be a compact and high performance solution for power converters and class D power amplifiers.

articleTitle: Tube size effect of anodized alumnium oxide template based gas sensor
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: The sensitivity of the anodized aluminum oxide (AAO) template based semiconductor metal oxide (SMO) gas sensor is closely related to the AAO's tube diameter size. In this work, a well-controlled ring-shaped AAO template is constructed in the simulation software and analyzed regarding its NO2 sensing behavior. For comparison, AAO tubes with different diameters of 500nm, 700nm and 900nm are constructed and the detailed I-Y curve and current density distribution figures are presented. According to the simulation results, it is indicated that the corresponding sensitivity increases from 1.59 to 2.57 as the tube diameter increases for 3×3 matrix. In addition, a uniform current density distribution in 3D surface is found in this template based sensing film together with the increased surface to volume ratio when the diameter is enlarged. Combining the above two reasons, we hereby conclude that AAO template based gas sensor with larger tube diameter can achieve a higher sensitivity due to the tube size effect. This study not only sheds light on the mechanism of performance enhancement with porous gas sensor structure, but also proposes a rational approach and a simulation platform to design this template based chemical/biology sensors with desirable performance.

articleTitle: A compact fast-transient charge-pump boost converter using hysteretic compensated techniques
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A compact charge-pump boost converter with fast transient response and high efficiency is presented in this paper. One inherent advantage of charge-pump boost converter is its fast transient response for load variation, and the other is current stress on the output capacitor of the charge-pump boost converter smaller than conventional boost converter. In order to improve the transient response, hysteretic compensated technique is chosen. The proposed converter was fabricated with a 0.35-μm CMOS process. The chip area is 1309μm × 1496μm. With an input voltage of 3.3V, the output voltage can be regulated from 3.6V to 5.1V. Furthermore, it achieves the peak efficiency of 93.2% under the condition of load current I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OUT</sub>=60mA. Experimental results demonstrate that transient response of this work is faster than other state-of-the-art designs. The measured transient response is only 4μs when the load current changes from heavy load to light load and vice versa.

articleTitle: High reliability multi-channel output voltage switch for multitime programmable memory in standard CMOS process
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This paper presents a row voltage switch and a column voltage switch for the multitime programmable (MTP) memories. In the standard CMOS process, without using any specially-designed Laterally-Diffused MOS (LDMOS) transistors, the proposed circuits can ensure that none of the devices gets overstressed which greatly improves the reliability and endurance of the circuits, and this is achieved by simply employing stacked latches and MOS switches. According to the post simulation results based on SMIC 0.13-μm standard CMOS process, the maximum delay time of the row and the column voltage switches are 11.15 ns and 9.48 ns, respectively, and the average power consumption within 2.5 ms are 309.5 nW and 485.3 nW, respectively. Furthermore, the proposed circuits achieve multi-channel output without any additional circuitry. In conclusion, the proposed circuits will have great advantages in applying to MTP memories.

articleTitle: Advanced physical models for widegap device simulation
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Wide bandgap materials such as SiC and GaN are regarded as second and third generations of semiconductors with potential to displace silicon in future power electronic applications. Simulation of wide bandgap devices within the framework of drift-diffusion theory poses unique challenges which we shall address in this paper. For SiC, we tackle the issue of numerical convergence at low temperatures as well as temperature dependent mobility model selection in a JBS structure. For GaN, interface and buffer layer traps are believed to be responsible for many pronounced effects such as reverse gate leakage and current collapse. We present formal theories and numerical simulation results related to trap effects in this paper. Experimental verifications are provided wherever available.

articleTitle: Manufacturing of using spray method to produce solar cell
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Solar power generation is a renewable and environmental friendly power generation approach without generating any greenhouse gas (such as carbon dioxide). Therefore, the solar cell production technologies have been booming and widely used in recent years. Generally speaking there are a variety of solar cells, the most frequently seen of which is silicon-based solar cell. The silicon-based solar cell is usually composed of P/N diode, anti-reflection layer, front contact electrode, and back contact electrode. When the electrons and holes of silicon atoms are excited by sunlight and set free, free electrons will be affected by the built-in electric field at P/N diode to speed up the separation, and the electrons and holes will be attracted to the metal wires on top and bottom terminals, thus forming the power generating and conducting loops. In this work dissertation a new production process of solar cell device has been proposed, in which semiconductor materials and dopants are grinded into powders before being mixed with conductive adhesives. And this mixture will be used for spraying or coating in the sequence of p-i-n to make solar cell. This production technique is different from the solar cell production technique with traditional solid state material as the substrate, which is limited by the failure in refining and control of size of dopant particle. The electrons and holes of the solar cell based on traditional solid state substrate material can only be excited by lights with certain high energy spectrum, and this factor has limited the enhancement of power conversion efficiency of silicon-based solar cell produced by traditional approach.

articleTitle: A versatile flicker noise measurement system and its applications in CMOS process
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A versatile multi-amplifier flicker noise measurement system with various programmable configurations was developed for accurate and fast on-wafer flicker noise measurement. The noise system performance, which includes system resolution, corner frequency and bandwidth, are thoroughly analyzed by correlating various system configurations, such as selection of LNAs, LNA noise floor, DUT output impedance, and parasitic stray capacitance of on-wafer prober. The system versatility and efficiency are also discussed. A few typical noise measurements are presented in the applications.

articleTitle: Quantum correction in AlGaN/GaN transistor simulations using Modified Local Density Approximation (MLDA)
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Highly degenerated and confined Two-Dimensional Electron Gas (2DEG) is the essential part of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs but is usually modeled classically. We studied the application of Modified Local Density Approximation (MLDA) as a quantum correction to 2DEG in AlGaN/GaN HEMTs. It is found that MLDA is an efficient model that does not degrade the convergence behavior with little run time penalty when the Poisson equation and electron/hole continuity equations are solved self-consistently. It is then applied to a power MISFET and a highly scaled N-polar HEMT for RF applications. It is found that by taking the quantum effect into consideration through MLDA, under certain bias conditions, the drain current can be changed by almost 10% and breakdown voltages are increased substantially. The f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub> can be changed significantly when gate over-drive is not sufficient.

articleTitle: Nanocarbon via interconnects
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: The continuous downward scaling in integrated circuit (IC) technologies has led to rapid shrinking of transistor and interconnect feature sizes. Scaling causes reduction in interconnect linewidth, which leads to surge in resistance due to increased contributions from grain boundary and surface scattering of electrons in the metal lines. Further, current density inside interconnects is also enhanced by the reduced linewidth and is approaching or exceeding the current-carrying capacity of the existing interconnect metals, copper (Cu) and tungsten (W). The resulting failure due to electromigration presents a critical challenge for end-of-roadmap IC technology nodes. Therefore, alternative materials such as nanocarbons and silicides are being investigated as potential replacements for Cu and W as they have superior electrical and mechanical properties in the nanoscale. In this review, the electrical properties of nanocarbons, in particular carbon nanotubes (CNTs), are examined and their performance and reliability in the sub-100 nm regime are assessed. Further, the measured properties are used to project 30 nm CNT via properties, which are compared with those of Cu and W.
